rules.title: Fair Chance in Housing Act - Ban on criminal record inquiries before conditional offer
rules.quote: A housing provider shall not require an applicant to complete any housing application that includes any inquiries regarding an applicant's criminal record prior to the provision of a conditional offer, except that a housing provider may consider whether an applicant has ever been convicted of drug-related criminal activity for the manufacture or production of methamphetamine on the premises of federally assisted housing, and whether the applicant is subject to a lifetime registration requirement under a State sex offender registration program.
rules.summary: Housing providers cannot ask about criminal records on rental applications or during the application process until after making a conditional offer, except for methamphetamine manufacturing convictions and lifetime sex offender registration.
rules.effective_date_evidence: This act shall take effect on the first day of the seventh month next following the date of enactment... Approved June 18, 2021.
rules.coverage_text: other than a dwelling unit in an owner-occupied premises of not more than four dwelling units
rules.exemption_note: Owner-occupied premises of not more than four dwelling units are exempt
rules.penalty: First violation: up to $1,000; second violation within 5 years: up to $5,000; two or more violations within 7 years: up to $10,000

rules.title: Fair Chance in Housing Act - Restrictions on consideration of criminal records after conditional offer
rules.quote: A housing provider shall not, either before or after the issuance of a conditional offer, evaluate an applicant based on any of the following types of criminal records: (1) arrests or charges that have not resulted in a criminal conviction; (2) expunged convictions; (3) convictions erased through executive pardon; (4) vacated and otherwise legally nullified convictions; (5) juvenile adjudications of delinquency; and (6) records that have been sealed.
rules.summary: Housing providers cannot consider arrests without conviction, expunged convictions, pardons, vacated convictions, juvenile records, or sealed records in tenant screening at any point in the process.
rules.effective_date_evidence: This act shall take effect on the first day of the seventh month next following the date of enactment... Approved June 18, 2021.
rules.coverage_text: other than a dwelling unit in an owner-occupied premises of not more than four dwelling units
rules.exemption_note: Owner-occupied premises of not more than four dwelling units are exempt
rules.penalty: First violation: up to $1,000; second violation within 5 years: up to $5,000; two or more violations within 7 years: up to $10,000

rules.title: Fair Chance in Housing Act - Time limits on consideration of convictions after conditional offer
rules.quote: After the issuance of a conditional offer to an applicant, a housing provider may only consider a criminal record in the applicant's history that: resulted in a conviction for murder, aggravated sexual assault, kidnapping, arson, human trafficking, sexual assault in violation of N.J.S.2C:14-2, causing or permitting a child to engage in a prohibited sexual act or in the simulation of such an act in violation of paragraph (3) of subsection b. of N.J.S.2C:24-4, or any crime that resulted in lifetime registration in a state sex offender registry; is for an indictable offense of the first degree that was issued, or if the conviction resulted in a prison sentence that sentence concluded, within the six years immediately preceding the issuance of the conditional offer; is for an indictable offense of the second or third degree that was issued, or if the conviction resulted in a prison sentence that sentence concluded, within the four years immediately preceding the issuance of the conditional offer; or is for an indictable offense of the fourth degree that was issued, or if the conviction resulted in a prison sentence that sentence concluded, within one year immediately preceding the issuance of the conditional offer.
rules.summary: After making a conditional offer, housing providers may only consider certain serious convictions without time limits, first-degree offenses within six years, second or third-degree offenses within four years, and fourth-degree offenses within one year.
rules.key_value: 6 years (1st degree), 4 years (2nd/3rd degree), 1 year (4th degree)
rules.effective_date_evidence: This act shall take effect on the first day of the seventh month next following the date of enactment... Approved June 18, 2021.

rules.exemption_note: Owner-occupied premises of not more than four dwelling units are exempt
rules.penalty: First violation: up to $1,000; second violation within 5 years: up to $5,000; two or more violations within 7 years: up to $10,000

rules.title: Fair Chance in Housing Act - Individualized assessment required for withdrawal of conditional offer
rules.quote: A housing provider may withdraw a conditional offer based on an applicant's criminal record only if the housing provider determines, by preponderance of the evidence, that the withdrawal is necessary to fulfill a substantial, legitimate, and nondiscriminatory interest.
rules.summary: Housing providers may only withdraw a conditional offer based on criminal history if they prove by preponderance of evidence that withdrawal serves a substantial, legitimate, and nondiscriminatory interest and perform an individualized assessment.
rules.effective_date_evidence: This act shall take effect on the first day of the seventh month next following the date of enactment... Approved June 18, 2021.

rules.title: Fair Chance in Housing Act - Ban on discriminatory advertising regarding criminal records
rules.quote: A housing provider shall not knowingly or purposefully publish, or cause to be published, any housing advertisement that explicitly provides that the housing provider will not consider any applicant who has been arrested or convicted of one or more crimes or offenses, except for drug-related criminal activity for the manufacture or production of methamphetamine on the premises of federally assisted housing, and whether the applicant is subject to a lifetime registration requirement under a State sex offender registration program.
rules.summary: Housing providers cannot publish advertisements stating they will not consider applicants with arrests or convictions, except for methamphetamine manufacturing and lifetime sex offender registration.
rules.effective_date_evidence: This act shall take effect on the first day of the seventh month next following the date of enactment... Approved June 18, 2021.

rules.title: Fair Chance in Housing Act - Ban on mandatory drug or alcohol testing
rules.quote: A housing provider shall not require an applicant to submit to a drug or alcohol test, or request the applicant's consent to obtain information from a drug abuse treatment facility.
rules.summary: Housing providers cannot require applicants to take drug or alcohol tests or request consent to obtain information from drug abuse treatment facilities.
rules.effective_date_evidence: This act shall take effect on the first day of the seventh month next following the date of enactment... Approved June 18, 2021.
